signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: CAD/JPY trades as the primary G10 expression of outperformance with the 1W average spread reaching a critical 1.594% threshold. CAD strength is underpinned by a positive ESI of +12.0 and a restrictive real policy rate of +0.15%, contrasting sharply with JPY's mildly accommodative real rate of -0.70%. While JPY bond yields are rising on BoJ hike expectations, the currency remains the G10 laggard with a -0.790% average weekly return. The 125bp OIS carry advantage further supports the CAD bid against a JPY still struggling with its trade deficit. Trade bias: Long CAD/JPY; strong G10 bilateral theme favors CAD outperformance. Catalyst: BoC meeting 9 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: BoJ surprises with an early hawkish pivot before the Sep 18 meeting, compressing the yield spread.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Carry + Technicals
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.21, holding below its SMA20/50 cluster (160.93/161.15) but remaining above the SMA200 at 158.12. The options market signals high conviction for downside protection with a strong 1M 25d risk reversal of -2.16, even as the 275bp Fed-BoJ carry differential supports the pair's floor. US CPI data matching forecasts at 0.1% for July has extended bearish USD momentum, yet JPY's safe-haven status remains broken as evidenced by the positive USD/JPY vs VIX correlation (z=+1.54σ). This setup suggests institutional players are paying for downside hedges against potential BoJ intervention at 160.00 while maintaining carry-positive positions. Trade bias: Neutral/range USD/JPY; strong downside options skew offsets carry support. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 48% hike priced). Risk: A sustained break back above 160.00 triggers BoJ/MoF verbal warnings or active intervention.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7078, maintaining a bullish posture above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (all below 0.7013). COT positioning shows leveraged funds are net long +37,990 (72.1% long), reflecting institutional alignment with the RBA's restrictive +0.60% real rate and the 72bp carry premium over USD. This institutional length is met by extreme retail divergence, with 79% of retail traders currently short, creating a high-conviction contrarian squeeze setup. Despite USD bears chasing totality post-CPI, the AUD long is reaching historical crowding levels which is likely to limit immediate upside. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; institutional and retail divergence supports trend continuation. Catalyst: Next RBA meeting 29 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: Retail capitulation and short-covering triggers a final blow-off top followed by a positioning-led reversal.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Volatility Risk Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3508, positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster following a 0.39% weekly gain. The options market is pricing a massive volatility risk premium with 1M IV at 11.0% vs a realized HV30 of 6.0%, creating a +5.0% spread. This suggests heavy institutional demand for protection against a break of the current range, as the Fed-BoE carry is currently neutral at 0bp. While speculative positioning is net long +39,039 (70.1% long), the extreme VRP indicates that the market is paying for tail-risk protection rather than outright trend conviction. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; extreme vol premium suggests a range-bound regime with high hedging costs. Catalyst: next BoE meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) 17 Sep — market bias hold. Risk: A sharp move in US yields following today's median CPI of +0.3% forces a directional breakout that justifies the high IV.

signals.title: NZD/USD — ESI Outperformance + Positioning Extreme
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5871 is underpinned by the strongest Economic Surprise Index in the G10 at +24.9, following a sustained run of data beats. This fundamental strength contrasts with extreme speculative positioning, where COT LF net is short -30,785 with a long percentage of only 9.7%. Despite the RBNZ's accommodative -1.56% real rate, the persistent data outperformance and the 125bp USD/NZD carry spread have created an asymmetric risk profile. The pair is currently testing its SMA20 at 0.5846, and a sustained hold above this level would signal a shift in sentiment against the crowded short. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD; data outperformance is mismatched with crowded spec shorts. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — market bias hike. Risk: RBNZ turns dovish despite the data beats, validating the existing speculative short bias.
